fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 has no linear syndrome realization: prime-ideal valuation of a sum is not the sum of column valuations, and trace/BCH postprocessing cannot restore that lost nonlinearity. Implementing the arithmetic by polynomial slacks or circuits re-enters O5 or O2, while the product formula does not imply large binary Hamming support.

Proposal 2 assumes the central missing object: a polynomial deterministic isolation family guaranteed to isolate an arbitrary nonempty witness set. No family, branch-selection matrix, fixed target, or mixed-sector completeness bound is specified; tiny affine-hash enumeration cannot discriminate that asymptotic derandomization claim.

Proposal 3 cannot provide the claimed canonical center. If a polynomially computable planar Pfaffian aggregate were nonzero exactly when the original SAT instance had a witness, it would already decide the source problem; otherwise cancellations and even witness counts destroy completeness, and the aggregate need not be an actual sparse matching indicator.

Proposal 4 remains inside the only formally open O7 niche but specifies no actual condenser matrices, quotient flags, field, multiplicities, or canonical tie-breaking, so there is no unique bounded experiment. Rank visibility is not Hamming support, and the required theorem must cover every mixed matrix while controlling worst-case YES weight and actual image rank.

Proposal 5 cannot be both global and polynomially linear. Explicitly listing global sections is exponential, while implementing group multiplication through local gates re-enters O1/O2; binary expansion also restores linear superpositions without any proved nonabelian support lower bound.

Proposal 6 supplies neither a polynomial-time generator construction nor a sparse universal YES representative. Truncated moment consistency risks O3 pseudoexpectations and O1 cube relations, while arbitrary mixed lifted evaluations require a theorem absent from the proposal; degree-2-to-4 tests cannot resolve the logarithmic-degree or output-rank regime.

Proposal 7 relies on nonlinear Gröbner reduction but O8 requires an explicit polynomial-size linear binary syndrome system. Explicit normal-form states can be exponential or NP-hard to compute, circuit compilation re-enters O2/O5, and known low-degree toric moves directly undermine the claimed long-move shield.

Across all seven proposals, no explicit polynomial-time H, target t, universal YES-cost bound, polynomial output-rank bound, and all-mixed-word NO invariant are supplied. Consequently none reaches the minimum specification needed for implementation or exact-transfer accounting.
evidence: The exchange-quotient verifier found 32 instances where illegal odd covers lie in the affine span of perfect matchings, including weight 5 versus matching weight 3. Global shells that become linear after encoding cannot merely identify or aggregate all legal witnesses.

Dense rank-oriented folds already exhibited the exact rank-versus-support failure relevant to Proposal 4: the frozen F8 condenser had no pointed kernels but worst YES 31 versus best NO 6. Generator-type folds, sparse hashes, and polar shortening also lost the finite gap.

The closest sparse-moment experiment, nonbacktracking Schur walks, achieved a finite ratio on selected tiny instances but had all-eight and holonomy illegal mixed words whose entire feature shell canceled. This is finite counterevidence to Proposal 6's mechanism, not an asymptotic theorem.

Direct integer exact cover proved only q versus q+2, and polynomial variable projection tables produced 12 versus 14. These results support the O5/baseline objection to valuation or normal-form implementations using ordinary integer auxiliaries.

The determinant/permutation dictionary retained short virtual states and required exponential monomial structure even after all compound states were added. This directly weakens both the Pfaffian-canonicalization and toric-normal-form routes.
No supplied verifier implements any of the seven proposed constructions, so none of their expected experimental moves is evidence.

fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 proves a nonlinear Laurent-polynomial certificate, not a polynomial-size linear syndrome or lattice encoding. Aggregated coefficients are polynomially many but degree-q functions of z; direct monomial lifting needs exponentially many products, while enforcing multiplication through an arithmetic tableau re-enters O2/O5. The bounded mixed-span test has no specified dictionary, cost, or correspondence to the original fiber.

Proposal 2 supplies no frozen evaluation family, number of blocks, field parameters, canonical labels, or binary matrix, so its experiment is not uniquely implementable. More fundamentally, PIT guarantees only that a nonzero mixed polynomial survives somewhere; simplex encoding then gives one constant-weight block and provides no theorem making every NO word heavier than worst-case YES.

Proposal 3 has no defined universally complete metric: a log-barrier Hessian detects proximity to nonnegativity faces, not integrality, and can heavily penalize edges used by valid matchings. The fractional polytope may be empty or lack the required relative interior, while rational rounding, centering, scaling, bit complexity, and an explicit integer Gram realization are unspecified. Optimizing lambda on tiny instances is post-hoc and not discriminating.

Proposal 4 does not specify transports, global paths, representation sectors, a binary generator, or a fixed target. Once legal sections are embedded in a binary linear fiber, odd sums of cheap legal lifts remain cheap pointed words; nonabelian multiplication does not prevent linear affine-closure cancellation after expansion.

Proposal 5 lacks a metric invariant connected to CVP distance. In a YES fiber, a signed cover z=z+-z- gives Az+=A(matching+z-), so the toric ideal relates its positive part to a legal matching after multiplication; Gröbner reduction depth is term-order/path dependent, and low-degree Markov moves directly threaten any claimed large filtration. Standard-monomial modules may also be exponential, with no polynomial-rank binary realization.

Proposal 6's combinatorial sparse-defect lemma is plausible but does not produce the required fixed-target linear selector. A polynomial-size dictionary cannot give distinct polylog-weight representations to all q! permutations by counting, while identifying many permutations restores rectangle/affine superpositions. No splitter, RS parameters, binary matrix, or complete mixed-span definition is frozen.

Proposal 7 is a multivalued phase lift without an explicit voltage rule, retained-character matrix, or binary conversion. Independent sheet choices create many cheap legal lifts whose odd linear superpositions can recreate illegal covers; enforcing coherence instead approaches the O4 coboundary obstruction or incurs a deck-size YES baseline.

Across all proposals, the proposed q≤4 tests cannot resolve polynomial output size, universal completeness, or asymptotic soundness. None supplies the explicit witness-oblivious matrix or integer basis, fixed target, rank bound, and every-mixed-word invariant required before O8 can apply.
evidence: The supplied affine-closure verifier found 32 instances where illegal odd covers lie in the affine span of perfect matchings, including weight 5 versus matching weight 3. This directly attacks the linearized nonabelian, selector, voltage, and global-shell mechanisms.

Prior noncommutative and dense folds already preserved nonzeroness while destroying support separation: the M3(F4) fold had NO pointed kernels, and the F8 condenser had worst YES 31 versus best NO 6 despite no kernels. Thus PIT/rank survival is not evidence of Hamming soundness.

Direct integer exact cover has only the proved q versus q+2 squared gap; variable projection tables yielded 12 versus 14. This supports the objection that global preconditioning or selector variables need a new norm theorem rather than finite tuning.

The determinant/global-algebra experiment retained short virtual permutations and exponential explicit state size even after all compound states were added. This is the closest supplied evidence against the Laurent and Gröbner linearization routes.

Exact mixed tensor soundness is already proved, but pure-power compression has a rigorous exponential dimension wall and tested sparse/dense folds lose the gap. Proposal 2 gives no mechanism escaping that rank wall.

No supplied verifier implements any of these seven proposals, and several experiments are not sufficiently specified to have a precommitted outcome. Finite success would not establish the claimed asymptotic mechanisms.
